after: ## Formation: the cases behind the rules
alt: Invitations to treat (shop shelves, windows, most advertisements) are contrasted with Carlill's unilateral offer. An offer box branches four ways: a counter-offer ends it (Hyde v Wrench), communicated revocation ends it (Routledge, Byrne, Dickinson), a request for information does not (Stevenson v McLean), and acceptance forms the contract (Felthouse: silence is not acceptance). Posted acceptance takes effect when posted, instantaneous when received.
caption: Counter-offer and revocation end an offer; a request for information does not; acceptance binds.

alt: Condition (Poussard v Spiers) and warranty (Bettini v Gye) are contrasted. Three steps test an exclusion clause: was it incorporated by signature, notice or course of dealing; which statute applies, UCTA for business contracts or the CRA for consumers; and does it survive. A table lists UCTA ss 2, 3 and 11 and CRA ss 31, 57, 62 and 65.
caption: Incorporated first, then tested against UCTA (business) or the CRA (consumer).

alt: Four routes to discharge: performance (Cutter v Powell, softened by Hoenig v Isaacs), agreement, breach including anticipatory breach (Hochster), and frustration (Taylor v Caldwell, Krell v Henry, but not mere expense, Davis Contractors). Below, misrepresentation can be fraudulent (Derry v Peek), negligent (s 2(1) Misrepresentation Act 1967) or innocent.
caption: Performance, agreement, breach or frustration; a misrepresentation can unpick the contract instead.

after: ## Privity, and why negligence is the alternative
alt: The consumer of the ginger beer had no contract with the manufacturer, shown by a crossed dashed line, yet an arrow shows the manufacturer owed her a duty of care in negligence, as in Donoghue v Stevenson. Cards cover privity (Tweddle, Dunlop) and the Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 1999.
caption: No contract with the manufacturer, but still a duty of care: negligence fills the privity gap.

alt: A timeline shows Leila's laptop screen failing at three weeks, inside the 30-day window for the short-term right to reject. Four steps: the rule (satisfactory quality, s 9), application, the remedy (s 20 rejection, or s 23 repair or replacement, then s 24), and that any exclusion of s 9 is not binding (s 31).
caption: Inside 30 days she can reject for a refund; otherwise repair or replace before s 24.
